title: Circuit-breaker-protected suggestion committer
creator: Aisha Gupta
description: Implement a circuit-breaker mediated committer for Optimize suggestions that enables incremental application of batching/caching recommendations while automatically halting and reverting when safety signals cross predefined thresholds. Goal is to reduce manual rollout toil and limit blast radius for auto-applied config changes. This task covers the controller changes, safety thresholds, transient state handling, runbook integration, and initial audit/metrics plumbing.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can accept a suggestion bundle and create a staged commit with metadata and trial cohort selectors
Circuit-breaker evaluates multiple live signals (latency p95, error rate, token-cost delta, and quality regressions) and prevents or pauses commits when thresholds are exceeded
Automated rollback triggers produce a revert commit and annotate the suggestion with reason + telemetry link
Operator UI surfaces pending commits with clear state, trial cohort membership, and recommended remediation actions
A/B cohort traffic slicing and seeding for initial trials is supported and configurable per-project
End-to-end tests exist for happy path, pause, abort, and delayed rollback scenarios
Initial rollout limited to beta customers via config flag and feature gate
Security review sign-off recorded and audit logs written to the central logging cluster
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged merge gated by security review. 2) Enable for internal staging with 1% traffic cohorts for 48 hours. 3) Monitor safety signals using test harness and synthetic workloads. 4) Expand to 5% for selected beta customers for 72 hours. 5) If stable, open to wider Dedicated tenants behind opt-in. Each stage requires green checks from telemetry and at least one SE/PM approval.
rollback_playbook: 1) Circuit-breaker auto-triggers rollback when thresholds breached. 2) Controller posts a revert commit, escalates to oncall via Slack + Ops runbook link, and pins the previous safe config. 3) Notify affected customers via support channel if customer_impact >= medium. 4) Create postmortem entry referencing implicated metrics and suggestion id. 5) Run hypothesis-driven test that reproduces failure in staging before re-attempting apply.
decisions: Use a lightweight state machine in the controller rather than a full workflow engine to keep latency low and reduce operational complexity
Primary safety signals are: p95 latency delta, 5xx error rate delta, per-token cost regression, and evaluation-set BLEU/ROUGE degradation where applicable
Rollback is optimistic and automated; human approval is required for re-apply attempts after auto-revert
Cohort selection uses sampling by team_id and route hash to avoid cross-tenant leaks and preserve reproducibility
